locations.name: Thebes (Luxor)
locations.description: Ancient Waset — capital of Upper Egypt during the New Kingdom. Karnak and the Valley of the Kings lie nearby.

locations.name: Memphis
locations.description: Capital of the Old Kingdom, near modern Mit Rahina south of Cairo.

locations.name: Giza
locations.description: Site of the Great Pyramid and Sphinx on the west bank of the Nile.

locations.name: Alexandria
locations.description: Founded by Alexander the Great; home of the Library and Pharos lighthouse.

locations.name: Amarna (Akhetaten)
locations.description: Akhenaten's capital Akhetaten at Tell el-Amarna; Amarna Period art and the Aten cult.

locations.name: Abydos
locations.description: Ancient Abdju — cult centre of Osiris and royal necropolis with the Temple of Seti I.

locations.name: Saqqara
locations.description: Memphite necropolis; site of Djoser's Step Pyramid and major Old Kingdom tombs.

locations.name: Heliopolis (Iunu)
locations.description: Ancient Iunu — principal cult centre of the sun god Ra; now Ain Shams in Cairo.

locations.name: Pi-Ramesses
locations.description: Ramesses II's Delta capital at Qantir; biblical Raamses and Exodus tradition.

locations.name: Tanis
locations.description: Ancient Djanet (San el-Hagar) in the northeastern Delta; royal tombs of the Third Intermediate Period.

locations.name: Edfu
locations.description: Ancient Djeba — Ptolemaic Temple of Horus, one of the best-preserved temples in Egypt.

locations.name: Aswan
locations.description: Ancient Swenet at Egypt's southern frontier; granite quarries and the island temple of Philae nearby.

locations.name: Hierakonpolis (Nekhen)
locations.description: Ancient Nekhen — early dynastic centre of Upper Egypt and site of the Narmer Palette.

locations.name: Kom Ombo
locations.description: Ancient Nubt — double temple of Sobek and Horus on the Nile north of Aswan.

locations.name: Babylon
locations.description: Capital of Hammurabi and Nebuchadnezzar on the Euphrates.

locations.name: Ur
locations.description: Sumerian city-state; birthplace of Abraham in biblical tradition.

locations.name: Nineveh
locations.description: Capital of the Assyrian Empire on the Tigris opposite modern Mosul.

locations.name: Uruk (Warka)
locations.description: One of the world's first cities; legendary home of Gilgamesh and centre of Inanna/Ishtar worship.

locations.name: Eridu
locations.description: In Mesopotamian tradition the oldest city; sanctuary of Enki/Ea near the Persian Gulf.

locations.name: Nippur
locations.description: Religious capital of Sumer; temple of Enlil (Ekur) conferred kingship legitimacy.

locations.name: Kish
locations.description: Early Dynastic city-state east of Babylon; in tradition the first seat of kingship after the Flood.

locations.name: Larsa
locations.description: Rival of Isin and Babylon in the early 2nd millennium BCE; centre of the sun-god Shamash.

locations.name: Assur (Ashur)
locations.description: Religious and early political capital of Assyria on the Tigris; namesake of the god Ashur.

locations.name: Nimrud (Kalhu)
locations.description: Assyrian capital under Ashurnasirpal II; biblical Calah south of Nineveh.

locations.name: Mari
locations.description: Euphrates city-state (Tell Hariri); palace archives document Mid-Bronze diplomacy.

locations.name: Ebla
locations.description: Powerful Early Bronze kingdom (Tell Mardikh); vast cuneiform archive of administration and trade.

locations.name: Ugarit
locations.description: Coastal capital (Ras Shamra); alphabetic cuneiform and Baal cycle myths; destroyed c. 1200 BCE.

locations.name: Aleppo (Halab)
locations.description: Capital of Yamhad in the Middle Bronze Age; enduring trade hub of northern Syria.

locations.name: Qatna
locations.description: Royal city of inland Syria (Tell Mishrife); ally and rival in Mitanni–Egyptian politics.

locations.name: Carchemish
locations.description: Euphrates fortress-city; Hittite viceroyalty and later Neo-Hittite capital on the modern Turkish–Syrian border.

locations.name: Washukanni
locations.description: Capital of the Mitanni kingdom (proposed at Tell Fekheriye near the Khabur headwaters).

locations.name: Alalakh
locations.description: Capital of Mukish (Tell Atchana) in the Amuq plain; under Mitanni then Hittite influence.

locations.name: Hattusa
locations.description: Capital of the Hittite Empire near modern Boğazkale; royal archives and the Yazılıkaya sanctuary.

locations.name: Troy (Ilion)
locations.description: Hisarlık mound on the Dardanelles; Homeric Ilion and major Late Bronze Aegean–Anatolian centre.

locations.name: Byblos (Gubla)
locations.description: Ancient coastal city of Lebanon; Egyptian timber partner and early alphabetic writing centre.

locations.name: Sidon
locations.description: Major Phoenician city-state on the Lebanese coast; trade and purple-dye industry.

locations.name: Tyre
locations.description: Island Phoenician metropolis; mother-city of Carthage and naval power of the Iron Age.

locations.name: Damascus
locations.description: Oasis capital of southern Syria; Aramean kingdom and one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities.

locations.name: Enkomi (Alashiya)
locations.description: Leading city of Bronze Age Cyprus (Alashiya); copper trade hub near modern Famagusta.

locations.name: Persepolis
locations.description: Ceremonial capital of the Persian Empire founded by Darius I.

locations.name: Susa
locations.description: Ancient Elamite and Persian administrative capital in Khuzestan.

locations.name: Athens
locations.description: Leading Attic polis; birthplace of democracy; Acropolis and Parthenon overlook the city.

locations.name: Sparta
locations.description: Dorian polis of Laconia; military rival of Athens and hegemon of the Peloponnesian League.

locations.name: Corinth
locations.description: Wealthy Isthmus polis controlling land and sea routes between mainland Greece and the Peloponnese.

locations.name: Thebes (Boeotia)
locations.description: Leading Boeotian polis; Cadmea citadel; briefly hegemon of Greece after Leuctra (371 BCE).

locations.name: Argos
locations.description: Ancient Argolid polis; rival of Sparta and heir to Mycenaean Argos in Greek tradition.

locations.name: Mycenae
locations.description: Citadel of Agamemnon; foremost Mycenaean palace centre of mainland Greece.

locations.name: Pylos (Nestor)
locations.description: Palace of Nestor in Messenia; rich Linear B archive of Late Bronze administration.

locations.name: Tiryns
locations.description: Mycenaean fortress with massive Cyclopean walls near the Argolic Gulf.

locations.name: Olympia
locations.description: Panhellenic sanctuary of Zeus in Elis; site of the ancient Olympic Games.

locations.name: Delphi
locations.description: Sanctuary of Apollo and the Pythia oracle on Mount Parnassus.

locations.name: Megara
locations.description: Isthmus polis between Athens and Corinth; mother-city of Byzantium and Chalcedon.

locations.name: Ephesus
locations.description: Ionian polis and sanctuary of Artemis; major Aegean port of Asia Minor.

locations.name: Rhodes
locations.description: Island polis of the Dodecanese; naval power and site of the Colossus.

locations.name: Syracuse
locations.description: Corinthian colony and leading Greek city of Magna Graecia; rival of Athens and Carthage.

locations.name: Knossos
locations.description: Palace of legendary King Minos; foremost centre of Minoan civilization near Heraklion.

locations.name: Phaistos
locations.description: Second great Minoan palace of southern Crete; findspot of the Phaistos Disc.

locations.name: Rome
locations.description: Caput Mundi — centre of the Roman Republic and Empire.

locations.name: Carthage
locations.description: Phoenician colony and rival of Rome on the Gulf of Tunis.

locations.name: Jerusalem
locations.description: Sacred city of Judaism, Christianity, and Islam.

locations.name: Jericho
locations.description: One of the oldest continuously inhabited settlements in the world.

locations.name: Palmyra
locations.description: Oasis city on the Silk Road between Rome and Persia.

locations.name: Petra
locations.description: Rose-red city carved in sandstone by the Nabataeans.

locations.name: Miletus
locations.description: Ionian city of Thales and Anaximander on the Aegean coast.

locations.name: Chang'an (Xi'an)
locations.description: Eastern terminus of the Silk Road and capital of several dynasties.

locations.name: Varanasi (Kashi)
locations.description: Sacred city on the Ganges, one of the oldest living cities.

locations.name: Angkor
locations.description: Capital of the Khmer Empire; Angkor Wat is the largest religious monument.

locations.name: Teotihuacan
locations.description: City of the Sun and Moon pyramids in the Valley of Mexico.

locations.name: Chichen Itza
locations.description: Maya-Toltec ceremonial centre on the Yucatán Peninsula.

locations.name: Tiwanaku
locations.description: High-altitude ceremonial centre on the shores of Lake Titicaca.

locations.name: Cusco
locations.description: Capital of the Inca Empire in the Peruvian highlands.

locations.name: Nazca
locations.description: Desert plain famous for geoglyphs visible from the air.
